title: Conflict and Peacemaking
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Conflict and peacemaking teaches that disagreements, offenses, and tensions must be handled with humility, truth, repentance, patience, and dependence on God. Biblical peacemaking seeks righteousness, not victory for self.
summary: Conflict and peacemaking teaches that disagreements, offenses, and tensions must be handled with humility, truth, repentance, patience, and dependence on God. Biblical peacemaking seeks righteousness, not victory for self.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Prince of Peace who reconciles sinners to God and teaches His people to pursue peace. His humility, truth, and mercy shape how believers handle conflict.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Conflict often reveals desires of the heart. James teaches that quarrels come from passions at war within people. Peacemaking therefore requires more than managing words; it requires humility before God.

Jesus gives a path for addressing sin directly and personally when possible. This protects relationships from gossip, avoidance, and public escalation before private faithfulness.

Biblical peacemaking is not passive. It speaks truth, seeks repentance, listens carefully, turns from pride, and aims at restoration where possible.

The peacemaker must also pursue humility. Scripture calls believers to count others more significant than themselves and to seek peace as far as it depends on them.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many conflicts become worse because people choose gossip, silence, defensiveness, or winning over humility. This doctrine calls believers back to Christlike peacemaking.

It also protects against false peace. Peace is not achieved by ignoring sin forever; it is pursued by truth, repentance, patience, and love.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: When conflict arises, examine your heart before God. Refuse gossip, listen carefully, speak truth humbly, confess your sin, and pursue peace where possible. Ask whether your goal is to honor Christ or simply to win.
